text: We present a square root law for active sensing of phase θ of a single pixel using optical probes that pass through a single-mode lossy thermal-noise bosonic channel. Specifically, we show that, when the sensor uses an n-mode covert optical probe, the mean squared error (MSE) of the resulting estimator θ<inf>n</inf> scales as 〈(θ-θ̂<inf>n</inf>)<sup>2</sup>〉 = O(1/√n) improving the scaling necessarily leads to detection by the adversary with high probability. We fully characterize this limit and show that it is achievable using laser light illumination and a heterodyne receiver, even when the adversary captures every photon that does not return to the sensor and performs arbitrarily complex measurement as permitted by the laws of quantum mechanics.

source.title: Fundamental limits of quantum-secure covert optical sensing
